metadata.case_name: CHAN KAN (OR KUN) AND ANOTHER v. YEUNG MING AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: Employed as an odd job worker by the Texas Cotton Mills Ltd.; also employed on a part-time basis by his father as a labourer in his transport business

injuries.description: a small haematoma and superficial abrasion over the forehead
source: (1) a small haematoma and superficial abrasion over the forehead

injuries.description: fractured shaft of the left femur
source: (2) fractured shaft of the left femur

injuries.description: a compound fracture of the lower and of left tibia and fibula, with loss of skin
injuries.body_part: left tibia and fibula (left lower leg)
source: (3) a compound fracture of the lower and of left tibia and fibula, with loss of skin.

manifestations.description: A number of scars on the forehead, the back of the left forearm, and on the left lower leg
Lower left leg markedly swollen with an open wound (1" in diameter) on the medial side of the leg in the ankle region, and a second wound (3" x 1") in the ankle region of the left foot
Two shallow unhealed ulcers antero-laterally and antero-medially measuring 1½ by ½ and 2 by ½
The ankle joint is fixed with 20o downward flexion
The left leg is 1½ shorter than the right
Permanent partial impairment of function estimated at 54% of the leg (equivalent to 27% of the whole man)
Used to play football and go swimming but will not now be able to play strenuous ball games

treatments_received: Insertion of a K nail for fractured femur
Fixation of the compound fracture by McKee's traction
Multiple re-admissions and further skin grafts (including 22nd March, 1978 and full thickness skin graft in April 1979)
Hospital care at Queen Elizabeth Hospital, Queen Mary Hospital and St. Theresa's Hospital

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: He used to play football and go swimming. He will not now be able to play strenuous ball games.
Multiple scars on forehead, back of left forearm and left lower leg; nasty extensive adherent scar with a thin layer of skin over the front of the left ankle; ongoing unhealed ulcers.
Brawny swelling of the left lower leg, ankle joint fixed with 20° downward flexion, and left leg 1½ shorter than right causing reduced mobility.
Field of work open to the 2nd plaintiff is drastically narrowed; only fit for some form of sedentary work and is unemployed; assessed loss of future earnings.
